decision_rule:
we say "SPHEREx separates A and B" only if, in
the real data, (1) the 68% profile interval of f_B (Delta chi2 <= chi2_red, i.e. errors
scaled for the model error) excludes both 0 and 1 in every epoch, (2) it is stable to
a 0.15 px shift of the assumed positions (the size of the WCS offsets we measured),
and (3) the SIMULATED fits recover a known pair and a known single star as different
(|mean f_B difference| > 3 x their scatter) with the PSF mismatch included.

decision.verdict: SPHEREx does not separate RW Aur A and B
failed_criteria: f_B interval (errors scaled by chi2_red) excludes 0 and 1 in only 6 of 10 epochs
with positions fixed, moving them by +-0.15 px moves the best f_B by up to 1.00
SIMULATED single vs pair with a 0.1 px PSF mismatch differ by only 0.7 x their scatter

interpretation: Plain answer: SPHEREx does not separate RW Aur A and B. RW Aur B sits 0.24 px (1.52") from A, a fifth of the ~1.3 px PSF core. Identifiability: with the position free the A and B fluxes are correlated at -0.997 to -0.924 per epoch (-0.92 to -0.87 even with the position known); only A + B is measured. The formal f_B errors look small (0.01-0.10) because RW Aur is very bright, but the best f_B per epoch runs from -0.18 to 1.14 (physical range 0-1), and with the positions fixed, moving them by +-0.15 px along the A-B line moves the best f_B to 0.0 one way and to >= 0.80 the other way, in every epoch: the 'split' is set by astrometry at the 0.15 px level, not by the light. Adding B lowers the joint chi2 by 2171 (534 after scaling by chi2_red) for 10 parameters, but SIMULATED epochs show why that is not a detection of B: a single star fitted with the pair model gives f_B = 0.10 +- 0.29 (exact PSF) and 0.24 +- 0.25 (PSF off by a 0.1 px blur), a true pair (f_B = 0.314) gives 0.35 +- 0.11 and 0.45 +- 0.16; the two cases differ by 0.7 x their scatter (n = 250 per case). The second component mostly soaks up ePSF shape error. The separation profile is not a robust measurement either: summed over epochs it is lowest at 1.6" (Gaia 1.52") with field stars fitted, but per epoch the minimum runs over 0.4-3.0" and without field stars the summed minimum is at the 3.0" grid edge. Joint vs per-epoch: one sky offset shared by all epochs fits worse (chi2_red 7.02 vs 3.55 with field stars; 14.57 vs 9.45 as published), so the per-epoch position offsets are real (WCS error between visits), not noise, and a joint position buys nothing. Ratio stability: the total-flux (A + B) ratios of the 8 published pairs agree with the aperture ratios to <= 1.7% (per-epoch) and <= 1.7% (joint pair) in every model, while A-only and B-only ratios move by up to 283% and 506% (per-epoch pair) or 42% and 273% (joint pair). So: the published blended (A + B) ratios stand; any statement about which component varied needs data that resolve the pair. Nothing published changes.
